claims.text: High-temperature structural and chemical stability is governed by formation of a stable, coherent interface between the nanoparticle and its surrounding environment.
A stable, coherent interface suppresses atomic diffusion.
A stable, coherent interface suppresses elemental segregation.
The coherent interface reduces interfacial energy.
The coherent interface increases the activation energy for atomic diffusion.
Suppression of diffusion and segregation maintains the solid-solution structure and composition.
Interface-stabilized nanoparticles will show a 25% increase in structural stability relative to the baseline.
The predicted structural-stability increase corresponds to lattice strain decreasing from 0.5% to 0.375%.
Interface-stabilized nanoparticles will show a 20% decrease in chemical instability relative to the baseline.
The predicted decrease in chemical instability corresponds to compositional variation decreasing from 5% to 4%.
The hypothesis applies to catalytic operation from 773 to 1173 K.
The hypothesis applies to thermoelectric operation from 473 to 1923 K.
The hypothesis is bounded to nanoparticles containing less than 10 at.% noble metal.
The hypothesis is bounded to nanoparticle sizes from 5 to 50 nm.
The hypothesis is bounded to inert or reducing atmospheres.

contradictions.description: The intervention includes oxidizing atmospheres, whereas the stated boundary limits applicability to inert or reducing atmospheres.
A decrease in lattice strain from 0.5% to 0.45% is exactly 10%, not less than 10% as stated.
A decrease in compositional variation from 5% to 4.75% is exactly 5%, not less than 5% as stated.
